prompt: Should the weekly working days be reduced and weekends extended? Give your opinion.
essay:
On the issue whether the amount of weekly work days should be reduced and thus weekends should be extended, I entirely agree. While politicians fear for productivity and economic stability, research has proven that employees with sufficient rest on the weekends are both more productive and more content. This has a measurable on the mental and physical health of workers, and thus affects the number of people requiring medical leave.

Recent studies have shown the effects of stress on the human brain. Prolonged periods of heightened anxiety can lead to symptoms resembling depression and insomnia. This can negatively influence the quality of work and lead to potentially disastrous consequences. While slightly cliche, the image of a surgeon being distracted during brain surgery is terrifying to most people, hence it serving as the plot of several episodes of medical TV dramas such as Grey’s Anatomy. While the fictional consequences seem overly dramatic, the reality can look surprisingly similar. This includes malpractice suits, terminations of work contracts or even lethal mistakes. These increased risks are another strain on the mental health of employees and form a vicious cycle, potentially ending in burnout and long term loss of employment. This will result in an increased demand for health insurance payouts, which will in turn be noticeable in higher taxes.

Physically, stress can affect virtually any part of the human body negatively. Apart from illnesses that are classified as psychosomatic, a high-stress environment can result in increased wear and tear on the body. Especially in rapidly paced, physically demanding jobs such as construction work, the employees need sufficient rest for their bodies to recuperate. Otherwise an increased risk of injury is evident from the health and safety authority’s annual reports. Here it states that muscle strains, injuries acquired due to overuse and fatigue were among the most common reasons given for workers who had to call in sick to work over the last five years. These injuries are likely to lead to an early retirement due to being unfit for further physical labour. This will result in a lack of labour available and a longer period of receiving state pensions, thus damaging the economy in the long term.

Conversely, a 2024 study from comparing Norway, Denmark and Germany exhibits the positive effect of longer weekends in a pilot programme in three cities in the respective countries. The workers report positive effects on mental and physical health, as well as overall motivation and contentment. Curiously, the companies involved show no decrease in productivity. The Danish insurance company even exhibited a slight increase in cases completed. Their internal survey on employee satisfaction supported the claims on the official study.

In conclusion, the mental and physical health of employees is paramount to ensure economic success and to reduce strain on society by limiting social benefits required. The sustained health of workers is affected by sufficient rest and therefore by longer periods of leisure. Thus, weekends should be extended.
